title: The most powerful and helpful app for building consistency in passion, and creating desired habits
body:
I’ve been trying to be productive and improve myself for almost 10 years now. Have tried many methods, apps, techniques, books, etc. I’ve become very productive for sure, but still I couldn’t become consistent in the things I wanted to do or I loved to do. Then enters this app in my life because of randomly searching productive apps to overcome my current weaknesses. It quickly became one of my most favourite app of these last 10 years. Streak numbers tell me how long I have come, and force me to continue my desired habits Continue in a healthy way. I can see my progress, edit my progress I missed to log by mistake, I can prioritise my habits by dragging them in different pages like first page for number 1 priority task, second for secondary priority tasks and so on. Ask though every single feature is my favourite, I want to give special thanks to shortcut feature. I created custom shortcuts using shortcut app, to start timer, close other apps, directly open desired app or multiple apps to work on that habit. For example: when I click on reading habit, it’ll close all other apps, start timer for few minutes or 1 pomodoro, open current book and current page, and silent notifications,etc. all in just one click from this Streak app itself. Now I don’t feel the need to create bookmark or move required aid to Homescreen. I just love this shortcut feature.

Improvement Suggestion: please give two different options to write shortcut name in habit setting. One for Mac shortcut name, one for I/Os shortcut name. So that when I click habit from Mac, it will run Mac shortcut. And if i run for m from iOS or iPadOS, it will run iOS shortcut. Because same created shortcut will be synced to all devices and streak habit will run shortcut on iOS/iPadOS properly but not in Mac as Mac shortcut and I/Os shortcuts are different. Currently it shows error.
Now i have disabled icloud sync of shortcuts and then edited mac shortcuts according to Mac. So it’s working for now. But Please find a workable solution for above mentioned issue. 

Thank you very much for creating such an amazing simple, intuitive and great app with awesome user experience.
Keep up the good work.

title: Repetition without logic
body:
You do 6 exercises daily. There are 4 levels to suit everyone’s convenience and body strength. It’s a good app to form daily habits but that’s the end of good part. 

Now the bad part.
There is no provision for breaks. So you do exercises one after the other without even 1 second of break in between. You can pause the timer but there is no in built break system. Then comes the part where they make you do the same exercise one after the other for short duration. So 5 push-ups, then 10 push-ups and 2 pushes rather than say, 10 push-ups and 7 push-ups consecutively. The problem is one has to focus again on the same exercise multiple time for short durations than for longer time but fewer times. I don’t get the logic. 
My last review was equally critical but never got published. I hope this one does.

title: Reliable and Easy
body:
There are two things I like about Streak:
1. All physical habits can be linked to other apps to track completion. For example, mindful minutes can be linked to any app that does meditation (I use Headspace) and as soon as you finish meditating, it’ll automatically update in Streaks. Similar for exercise, water intake, sleep, etc - which is very helpful. 

2. It limits you to a max of 12 habits which is so helpful for enthusiastic sorts like me who get carried away.

title: Great application!
body:
First, I underestimated its impact. People talk about gamification and other buzz words, but these folks have shown how that can be used to help improve our habits. For the first time in my life, I have continuously brushed before I sleep 90 percent of the time in the past month. Even my walking and reading habits have improved. This app genuinely benefitted me. Thanks for that.

Next, I am a designer myself and I think that this app is well designed. It looks ookay, but every detail that is needed to do what you have to is taken care of. The options are never in sight until needed, but are obvious when you need them. For instance, after adding my tasks to walk, read and brush, I realized that I have to reminded of these at different times (evening, before I sleep and after dinner). When I searched, the option was there. Similarly, these days, I brush but forget to mark it before I sleep. The next day, when I open the app and try to mark, it asks me about the day before too. Similarly, when I've consistently met my walking target, it asked me if it should increase the daily target steps. Thats neat!

I don't usually write long reviews, but this app deserves it!
